strings.name: Nadia Comăneci
strings.role: Gymnast · Pioneer of the Olympic perfect ten
strings.summary: Comăneci became the first gymnast to receive an Olympic perfect ten at Montreal 1976, changing the sport's international visibility with precise, difficult routines. She earned five golds among nine Olympic medals, retired in 1984 and left Romania in 1989. Later based in the United States, she supported gymnastics education and charity. In 2026 she received Laureus lifetime recognition and returned to Montreal for the fiftieth anniversary.
strings.coverageNote: Selected verifiable milestones through November 16, 2026; not a live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Her Olympic perfect scores transformed gymnastics' global reach and made her an enduring cultural symbol of the sport.

strings.highlights.h1.title: First Olympic perfect ten
strings.highlights.h1.text: Received the first Olympic gymnastics ten on uneven bars in 1976.
strings.facts.f2.label: Education and early training
strings.facts.f2.value: Trained in Onești under Béla and Márta Károlyi and entered elite gymnastics as a child.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Five Olympic golds
strings.highlights.h2.text: Earned nine medals, including five golds, across the 1976 and 1980 Games.

strings.timeline.t1.text: Attended fiftieth-anniversary commemorations and spoke to the press.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Laureus lifetime award
strings.timeline.t2.text: Received lifetime recognition at the Madrid awards ceremony.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Leaves Romania
strings.timeline.t3.text: Crossed the border before the change of regime and later settled in the United States.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Formal retirement
strings.timeline.t4.text: Ended competitive gymnastics and moved toward teaching and promotion.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Two Moscow golds
strings.timeline.t5.text: Won balance beam and floor exercise gold medals.
strings.timeline.t6.title: World team champion
strings.timeline.t6.text: Helped Romania win its first women's world team title.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Montreal perfect score
strings.timeline.t7.text: Scored ten on bars; earned seven tens and three golds at those Games.
strings.timeline.t8.title: European breakthrough
strings.timeline.t8.text: Won the all-around and three apparatus titles at the Skien Europeans.
strings.timeline.t9.title: National championship debut
strings.timeline.t9.text: Entered Romania's national championships as a child and gained competition experience.
